panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Gross excisional specimen of a large well-circumscribed right breast mass with bosselated surface, consistent with giant juvenile fibroadenoma. Caption and article title support disease attribution. B: Cut surface of the excised right breast mass showing lobulated, creamy white fibroadenomatous tissue with slit-like spaces and cystic change, consistent with giant juvenile fibroadenoma. Caption supports the specific findings.
panels.attribution_text: Baral et al. Giant juvenile fibroadenoma in an adolescent female: A case report.. Clinical case reports 2020. doi:10.1002/ccr3.3466. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 3.
panels.figure_caption: Showing the excisional biopsy of the right breast lump measuring approximately (9 × 7 × 6.5) cm, firm, well‐circumscribed, ovoid creamy white with bosselated surface. Cut surface shows slit‐like spaces along with two cystic spaces and lobulations bulging over the cut surface
in_text_mentions: y lesion with lobulated margin in the peri‐areolar region of the right breast (Figure 2). The patient was taken for surgery, and enucleation of the tumor was done with inframammary incision along the right breast. Intraoperatively, the tumor was 9 cm × 7 cm in size, firm, ovoid, well circumscribed with bosselated surface with nodularity. Cut section of the mass showed many slit‐like spaces with gray white in color (Figure 3). Postoperative event remained uneventful. The patient got discharged on 4th postoperative day. Histopathology was consistent with complex juvenile fibroadenoma (Figure 4).

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Panel A is an H&E microscopic section of the excised right breast mass from an adolescent girl; the caption and in-text describe benign ducts with a double epithelial/myoepithelial layer in fibrous stroma, confirming giant juvenile fibroadenoma. B: Panel B is a second H&E section of the same excised right breast mass, showing fibroepithelial architecture with benign ducts in fibrous stroma consistent with the confirmed giant juvenile fibroadenoma.

in_text_mentions: Microscopic examination revealed numerous benign ducts lined by a double layer of epithelial and myoepithelial cells, without evidence of atypia. The background consisted of fibrous stroma, and no features suggestive of malignancy were identified. These findings confirmed the diagnosis of giant juvenile fibroadenoma. Figure 4A,B shows representative histological sections of the lesion.Fig. 4A, B Microscopic images of the excised right breast mass

panels.rationale: Single-panel H&E photomicrograph from a case report titled 'Bilateral giant juvenile fibroadenoma of breasts'; the figure shows a biphasic fibroepithelial proliferation with increased stromal and epithelial (parenchymal) cellularity, matching juvenile fibroadenoma histology, and the caption explicitly states there is no focal periductal concentration of cells (i.e., no phyllodes pattern). No patient demographics or ethnicity are given in the caption or in-text mentions.
panels.attribution_text: Mukhopadhyay et al. Bilateral giant juvenile fibroadenoma of breasts.. Journal of Indian Association of Pediatric Surgeons 2009. doi:10.4103/0971-9261.55156. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 3.
panels.figure_caption: Histopathology (H and E Stain; Photomicrograph- 10 × 10) shows increased cellularity of Stromal and parenchymal component. no periductal concentrates of cells
in_text_mentions: ere was no evidence of malignancy. Excision of bilateral breast lumps conserving the normal breast tissues along with nipple and areola was done. Cut surface of the lumps were solid, grayish white and bulging with whorled appeareance. Hematoxylin and eosin (H and E) stain showed [Figure 3] increased cellularity of stromal and parenchymal component. Stromal cellularity was increased but there was no focal periductal concentrate of cells; a characteristic of phyllodes tumor. The patient is on regular follow-up and doing well at six months follow-up. We do not plan prosthesis or augmentation now.

Attribution is limited because the cytologic appearance is non-specific and the caption does not itself name the disease, hence moderate-to-low confidence; no skin is visible so skin tone is null, and age/ethnicity are not stated in the caption or provided text.

in_text_mentions: Ultrasound examination of the breast showed a hypoechoic mass in the outer half of the right breast. Its maximum diameter measured 10 cm, with significant internal vascularity. Breast MRI indicated a firm mass, with clear margins and characteristics of a benign mass, most probably a giant fibroadenoma. Its dimensions were calculated as 7.4 cm × 6 cm × 8.1 cm (Figure 2).

in_text_mentions: ained that her left breast was larger than the right breast and she had been able to feel a mass in her left breast for 2 months. She was admitted to our hospital on February 19, 2017, with no history of trauma, nipple discharge, fever, or weight loss. On physical examination, enlargement of the left breast with one palpable mass was observed (Fig. 1). The mass was about 6 × 6 cm, movable, solitary, firm, and well defined. It was not tender and did not adhere to the skin or the underlying structures. The local temperature of the overlying skin was normal. There was no axillary lymphadenopathy.

Breast ultrasound demonstrated a homogenous, hypoechoic solid mass with no phyllodes. Mammography showed a large mass with high density and well definition (Fig. 1). Based on the clinical and experimental findings, the mass was considered a giant fibroadenoma. Due to the history of progressive enlargement of the left-sided lesion, she underwent an excision biopsy instead of needle biopsy. To avoid a disfiguring scar, we planned to use the 8-gauge Mammotome to shrink the mass and then perform the lumpectomy through a tiny circumareolar incision.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: This is a mammogram (radiograph) showing a low-density, large, well-defined mass with lobulated margins in the right breast, consistent with the diagnosis of giant juvenile fibroadenoma, which is the focus of the case report. B: This MLO mammogram (radiograph) is a continuation of the same clinical presentation shown in Panel A, depicting a large, lobulated mass within the context of dense fibro-glandular tissue, which supports the diagnosis of giant juvenile fibroadenoma.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: The image is a histopathology slide demonstrating the characteristic biphasic (epithelial and stromal) architecture of complex juvenile fibroadenoma, consistent with the article's diagnosis. B: This high-power view of histology illustrates glandular epithelial structures characteristic of fibroadenoma formation. C: Histological view confirming the presence of epithelial elements within the mass. D: Histopathological view showing the supportive stromal tissue of the lesion.

The patient was taken for surgery, and enucleation of the tumor was done with inframammary incision along the right breast. Intraoperatively, the tumor was 9 cm × 7 cm in size, firm, ovoid, well circumscribed with bosselated surface with nodularity. Cut section of the mass showed many slit‐like spaces with gray white in color (Figure 3). Postoperative event remained uneventful. The patient got discharged on 4th postoperative day. Histopathology was consistent with complex juvenile fibroadenoma (Figure 4).
